Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

when conjunction

at the time that (not the question)

also as (when), once (when)

classical

Ter. And. 309: Facile omnēs, cum valēmus, rēcta cōnsilia aegrōtīs damus.
Quint. 1.9.5: cum indoctum puerum vīdisset, paedagōgum ejus percussit

cum

conjunction: the indicative for the time pure and simple (present, future, and things that happen again and again); in past narrative the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive

“When he had seen …” in a story is cum vīdisset; “when you come” is the future perfect, cum vēneris, as after sī (see if).

Other words

  • ubi — when, as soon as

    conjunction, with the indicative (perfect in narrative) · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 6.14: quem ubi vīdī, equidem vim lacrimārum prōfūdī (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. 1.30.1: humilēs labōrant ubi potentēs dissident

  • ut — when, as soon as

    conjunction, with the perfect indicative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.1.3: ut vēnī in Arpīnās

Examples

  • Facile omnēs, cum valēmus, rēcta cōnsilia aegrōtīs damus.

    When we are well, we all find it easy to give good advice to the sick.Ter. And. 309

  • istō bonō ūtāre, dum adsit; cum absit, nē requīrās

    make use of that good while you have it; when it is gone, do not pine for itCic. Sen. 33

  • ut Cratēs, cum indoctum puerum vīdisset, paedagōgum ejus percussit

    as Crates, when he had seen an ignorant boy, struck the boy’s tutorQuint. 1.9.5

  • quem ubi vīdī, equidem vim lacrimārum prōfūdī

    when I saw him, I burst into tearsCic. Rep. 6.14 (Lewis & Short)

  • ut vēnī in Arpīnās, cum ad mē frāter vēnisset, in prīmīs nōbīs sermō isque multus dē tē fuit

    when I arrived at Arpinum and my brother had come to me, our first talk, and a long one, was about youCic. Att. 5.1.3

See also whenever, after, as soon as, while.

SourcesLewis & Short: cum · Lewis & Short: ubi · Lewis & Short: ut
